controls.notes: Office versus Office Group. The Office Group option is greyed on Routing Slip and the four Ledger reports (mode locked to office); the whole control is greyed on Referral Source List.

108 = id of the office the user was working in (token working_office). Executive Summary: one KPI block per resolved office (fixed outer group level office, always applied, also for a single office); figures are the activity within that office - production, visits and procedures by office of service (rpt_charges.office_id / rpt_visits.office_id), payments and adjustments by transaction office (rpt_ledger_entries.office_id), appointments by appointment office, A/R block per office with allocation unit account_office. Exception (vendor documentation): the new-patient counts use the patient's home office (rpt_patient_dim.home_office_id). The vendor-recommended run selects all offices; whether a consolidated all-offices block is appended is unverified - check on the live tool.

Limits every figure to the selected providers; ALL echoed as 'Providers : ALL'. Provider column per figure (no single attribution): production, procedures and non-visit transactions = treating provider rpt_charges.provider_id; patients seen / patient visits = rpt_provider_visits.provider_id; missed / cancelled appointments and chair hours = rpt_appointment_facts.provider_id; collections and collection adjustments = provider on the ledger leg rpt_ledger_entries.provider_id (credited provider, not the allocation provider). The per-figure binding is inferred: the vendor documents only that the picker limits the figures - confirm on the live tool with a two-provider office. Declared parity exceptions to PD-7: collections by the ledger-leg provider (enhancement collections_provider_attribution = allocation_provider offers the PD-7 basis) and hygienist credit = treating provider. Show AR block: filtered on rpt_ar_open_items.provider_id (inferred). New-patient lines and the Referrals block are not provider-limited (inferred).

Primary date range, fixed date_basis transaction_date (04 7.2 row 26, documented: production uses the posting date). Charges carry transaction_date = service date until DATA-13. The MTD and YTD blocks derive from date_to only (MTD = first of that month through date_to, YTD = January 1 through date_to). New Patients uses the patient created date (unreliable for migrated patients: load timestamp), New Patients by First Visit Date uses the first visit date. Default today in the office time zone; enhanced with presets and relative tokens.

Inclusive end of the transaction-date range; also the as-of date of the Show AR block and the end of the MTD / YTD windows. Default today in the office time zone; enhanced with presets and relative tokens.

Executive Summary: adds the block 'A/R as of : <date_to>' (Current / Over30 / Over60 / Over90 / Over120 / Total A/R, then Estimated Insurance and Estimated Patient) per office, computed from rpt_ar_open_items(:tenant_id, :date_to, NULL, 'account_office') and the footer flag '* Show AR.'. role: query (the block is computed only when ticked; escalates to background with more than one office or a tenant-wide scope). Legacy bucket set; buckets carry open debits, credits are netted into Total A/R only (legacy placement of credits unverified). The block is as of date_to for any range; the vendor says it matches the Aging Report only for a single-day run - whether the legacy as-of differs on multi-day runs is to be confirmed on the live tool. Enabled on this report.

None = office totals; Provider = the KPI block repeated under a provider header inside each office (layout inferred, third-party source). Provider-grouped visit counts read rpt_provider_visits and are not additive across providers (a patient-day seen by a dentist and a hygienist counts under both); the office total still comes from rpt_visits.

Page Break checkbox beside GROUP BY: ticked sets page_break_by = group (each provider block starts a new PDF page; layout role, the snapshot is reused). Greyed while GROUP BY = None; Provider is the only other value, so enabled_when group_by == provider (inferred from the criteria screen). Member checkbox: default false = unticked, so page_break_by = none (the parity default and the Shared-rules value 'none' are the same state).

Show AR adds an A/R snapshot whose as-of date is the END of the report range (End Date); it matches the Aging report only when the Executive Summary is run for a single day.
Show AR is off by default (vendor text). Ticking it adds the `A/R as of` block to the report and the footer flag `* Show AR.`; without it no A/R figures print.

Start Date / End Date give the range for the counts and the money figures. The MTD and YTD blocks are derived from the End Date alone: MTD = first day of that month through the End Date, YTD = January 1 through the End Date.

One KPI block is printed per selected office, and the figures reflect the activity within that office.

On this report the selected office(s) are HOME offices: it lists the responsible parties whose home office is selected and considers all of their transactions wherever they were recorded.
Report Date is the single as-of date of the ageing (not a range); ageing starts when a procedure is marked completed.
Start Name / End Name are an alphabetical range on the responsible party LAST name.
AGING BY = Account AR counts the insurance + patient balances on the account and can include balances that belong to another office (for example a dependant whose home office differs).

The five bucket checkboxes (Current, Over 30, Over 60, Over 90, Over 120) are an ACCOUNT filter: they select the accounts that have a balance in a ticked bucket.
Include Credit Balance adds the accounts whose total is negative; left unticked (the default) credits are left out and the grand total is higher than the real A/R.
SHOW ONLY CREDIT BALANCES lists only the accounts with a negative total.

Include Balance Status prints the account's Balance Status - a tenant-defined collections-stage note (10-character code + description) set with the Ledger's Balance Stat button and maintained in Setup > Misc Setups > Balance Status.
Include Contract Balances adds the remaining payment-contract balances (regular / ortho contracts keep their balance off the ledger until the periodic charges post).

PRINT FORMAT = Excel downloads a flat spreadsheet (one record per row) instead of opening the PDF viewer, and the Excel layout can carry columns the PDF does not - here the extended buckets behind `Over 120+`.
PATIENT TYPE restricts the report to general or to ortho patients (Both = no restriction); the choice is echoed in the report footer.
EXCLUDE RESP. PARTY TYPE drops the accounts of the selected responsible-party types; the selection is echoed in the report footer as `Ex Resp Party Type`.
This option drops the accounts whose remaining balance is expected entirely from insurance.

Bucket boundaries in days, as the vendor defines them: Current = 0-29 (article) or 0-30 (glossary); Over 30 = 30 or 31 to 59; Over 60 = 60 or 61 to 89; Over 90 = 90 or 91 to 119; Over 120 = 120 and more, or more than 120. The vendor's two definitions differ by one day at the boundaries.

For this report the conclusion rests on its panel being pixel-identical to Aging Report by Home Office, under which the document reports the vendor screenshots.
The two clipped option labels are confirmed as read: `Resp. Party Last name` and `Resp. Party ID`. The [?] markers of the inventory can be dropped.

On this report the selected office(s) are TRANSACTION offices: only the transactions recorded in the selected office(s) are evaluated (unlike Aging Report by Home Office, which has the same criteria panel).
Report Date is the single as-of date of the ageing (not a range); ageing starts when a procedure is marked completed.
Start Name / End Name are an alphabetical range on the responsible party LAST name.
AGING BY = Account AR counts the insurance + patient balances on the account and can include balances that belong to another office (for example a dependant whose home office differs).
AGING BY = Patient AR counts only the patient balances for this office; accounts that only have an estimated insurance balance do not appear.
The five bucket checkboxes (Current, Over 30, Over 60, Over 90, Over 120) are an ACCOUNT filter: they select the accounts that have a balance in a ticked bucket.
Include Credit Balance adds the accounts whose total is negative; left unticked (the default) credits are left out and the grand total is higher than the real A/R.
SHOW ONLY CREDIT BALANCES lists only the accounts with a negative total.

Include Balance Status prints the account's Balance Status - a tenant-defined collections-stage note (10-character code + description) set with the Ledger's Balance Stat button and maintained in Setup > Misc Setups > Balance Status.
Include Contract Balances adds the remaining payment-contract balances (regular / ortho contracts keep their balance off the ledger until the periodic charges post).

REPORT FORMAT: Detail = one block per account (responsible party); Summary = office totals - the vendor describes it as the A/R snapshot of the outstanding patient and insurance balances of each selected office.

PRINT FORMAT = Excel downloads a flat spreadsheet (one record per row) instead of opening the PDF viewer, and the Excel layout can carry columns the PDF does not - here the extended buckets behind `Over 120+`. Documented for the aging criteria panel under Aging Report by Home Office; the document states that the Aging Report panel is identical and that every option behaves the same.

PATIENT TYPE restricts the report to general or to ortho patients (Both = no restriction); the choice is echoed in the report footer. Documented for the aging criteria panel under Aging Report by Home Office; the document states that the Aging Report panel is identical and that every option behaves the same.

EXCLUDE RESP. PARTY TYPE drops the accounts of the selected responsible-party types; the selection is echoed in the report footer as `Ex Resp Party Type`. Documented for the aging criteria panel under Aging Report by Home Office; the document states that the Aging Report panel is identical and that every option behaves the same.

This option drops the accounts whose remaining balance is expected entirely from insurance. Documented for the aging criteria panel under Aging Report by Home Office; the document states that the Aging Report panel is identical and that every option behaves the same.

Bucket boundaries in days, as the vendor defines them: Current = 0-29 (article) or 0-30 (glossary); Over 30 = 30 or 31 to 59; Over 60 = 60 or 61 to 89; Over 90 = 90 or 91 to 119; Over 120 = 120 and more, or more than 120. The vendor's two definitions differ by one day at the boundaries.

controls.notes: Detail = one line per allocation (payment or collection adjustment against a procedure) with Pay Date, Allo Date and Proc Date, grouped by provider (layout inferred, PARTIALLY DOCUMENTED); Summary = one row per provider (zero rows included) plus an Unallocated row and a Total row, with the roll-forward columns Beginning Balance ... Ending Balance, Non Income, Income (documented). Legacy default Detail kept.
Office versus Office Group. The Office Group option is greyed on Routing Slip and the four Ledger reports (mode locked to office); the whole control is greyed on Referral Source List.

108 = id of the office the user was working in (token working_office); several offices or an office group allowed. Income Allocation: the selected offices are ALLOCATION offices - money is credited to the office where the paid procedure was charged (rpt_payment_allocations.allocation_office_id), not the office where the payment was entered. The Unallocated row (method = unallocated, no debit) is attributed to the credit's own office (credit_office_id) - inferred, confirm on the live tool.

Allocation provider: the provider of the completed work the money was allocated to (rpt_payment_allocations.allocation_provider_id). NULL prints as a separate 'Unassigned provider' row, which is not the Unallocated row. Not the provider on the payment line. ALL = no restriction; the Unallocated row is printed only under ALL - a builder rule, not an enabled_when, and inferred (it belongs to no provider): confirm on the live tool.

Primary date range, fixed date_basis created_date (04 7.2 row 28, documented; supersedes the coverage matrix's 'allocation date'). Dating per roll-forward column: payments, prev_allocation, prev_allocation_prod_adj, income_adjust_neg, prev_allocation_income_adj by the credit's created date (credit_created_date; prev columns: created before date_from, allocated in range); income_adjust_pos, non_income and transfer legs by their created_date; charges, production adjustments and unclassified_adjust by transaction_date (inferred). A payment entered Feb 1 and back-dated to Jan 15 falls in February. Beginning Balance is as of date_from - 1, Ending Balance as of date_to. Migrated money rows carry the load timestamp as created_at until the created-date restore (REPAIR(10)); the run prints an availability warning for ranges before the migrated-through date. Enhanced with presets and relative tokens.
Inclusive end of the created-date range (see Start Date); also the as-of date of Ending Balance. Default today in the office time zone; enhanced with presets and relative tokens.

legacy_corrections.text: Start Date / End Date are matched against the CREATED (entry) date of the payment, not the editable transaction date: a payment entered Feb 1 and back-dated to Jan 15 appears in February.
The office box defaults to the logged-in office; several offices or an office group can be selected for one run.

Money is credited to the office where the procedure was charged (the production / allocation office), not to the office where the payment was entered - so the selected offices are the offices where the treatment was charged.
REPORT FORMAT = Summary: one row per provider, then an Unallocated row and a Total row - the vendor's basis for collection-based provider pay.

REPORT FORMAT = Detail: the individual lines, each with its Pay Date, Allo Date (allocation date) and Proc Date; the vendor uses it to find back-dated payments and payments made outside the date range yet allocated inside it.
Provider here is the provider whose completed work the money was allocated to (the allocation provider), not the provider the payment was entered under.
The absence of a PRINT FORMAT section is real (as captured): the output is exported from the report viewer instead.

Vendor text about the "Allocation report", which the document reads as the older name of this report.
Date basis of the allocation report family (Income Allocation / Allocation): the created (entry) date of the payment, not its editable transaction date.

Allocation reports attribute a payment to the office and the provider whose work it paid, not to the office / provider it was entered under (stated for the allocation reports as a family). That the OFFICE/GROUP and Provider selections of this report follow the same attribution is implied, not stated.

controls.notes: true = the date range is ignored and every credit that is unallocated as of the office-local today is listed (as-of snapshot); the two date boxes are disabled (enabled_when on date_from / date_to, 04 rule). false (legacy default) = credits entered in the range that are still unallocated today.

true = drop the unallocated items of accounts whose total balance (rpt_ledger_entries sum per account) is a credit, leaving the credits that sit unapplied while the account still owes - the posting errors to fix (meaning inferred from vendor text 'credit balances can be excluded'). On derived allocations every unallocated row is a credit balance by construction, so a ticked run is empty until DATA-26 persists allocations with reasons. The account balance is taken as of the office-local today (the unallocated state is today's).

false = drops lines whose credit patient has rpt_patient_dim.is_active = false (inferred; inactive and deleted share the flag until DATA-44); true = no patient-status predicate. Confirm on the live tool whether the paying patient or the account is tested.

Primary date range, fixed date_basis service_date (04 7.2 row 32, documented): selects the service months of the production (service_date of the debit leg) that form the rows; the month columns are the months in which credits were applied to that production (allocation_date), up to the run date - column window inferred. A partial first or last month is clipped to the range for both billed_amount and the cells. 'Use a range of at least one quarter' is vendor guidance, shown as a UI hint (enhancement). Enhanced with presets and relative tokens.
Inclusive end of the service-date range. Default today in the office time zone; enhanced with presets and relative tokens.

Which credits fill the cells: payments_only = credit_entry_type patient_payment / insurance_payment with credit_ledger_bucket = 'collection'; adjustments_only = credit_entry_type adjustment (write-offs included); payments_and_adjustments = the union of the two, so the two subsets add up to it. Opening-balance and transfer credits (APBAC / APBIC, transfer legs) and non-collection payments are in no option. Whether contractual write-offs count as adjustments here is not documented - confirm on the live tool.
